- Confusables and KG hints, Section Six Navigating the Roads","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 - Confusables and KG hints, Section Six Navigating the Roads

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
A lone solid yellow center line forbids passing only when your direction holds a single lane and that line sits on your side, whereas double solid yellow lines forbid every crossing except HOV entrances, signed detours, and left turns or U-turns over one set. Twin sets spaced two or more feet apart form a barrier no turn may cross except at openings [A01].
Why it matters: group lane-markings; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F01, sec06-F02, sec06-F03 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A02
Double solid white lines wall off preferential lanes and ramp edges and must never be crossed, while oversized broken white lines warn a lane is ending and yield triangles of white point at drivers who must stop or yield [A02].
Why it matters: group lane-markings; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-R01; confusables sec06-F04, sec06-F05 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A03
Numbered lanes count outward from the fast Number 1 lane on the left, so passing and left turns belong left while entering and exiting belong right, and a missed turn means driving on to a legal turnaround rather than a last-second swerve [A03].
Why it matters: group lane-choice; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec06-F06, sec06-F07 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A89
HOV lanes admit only posted carpools, buses, decal low-emission vehicles, and motorcycles through marked entries, unlike the center left-turn lane which any driver may borrow for at most two hundred feet to turn, and slow two-lane traffic must yield at turnouts once five or more followers stack up [A89] [A98].
Why it matters: group special-lanes; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R03; confusables sec06-F08, sec06-F09 [A89].
Source: [A89 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A05
Bike lanes stay exclusive to cyclists apart from parking, entering, leaving, or turning within two hundred feet, and drivers must still scan blind spots, treat motorized bikes gently, and keep three feet from every rider [A05].
Why it matters: group bike-lanes; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F10, sec06-F11 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A06
Prepare a right turn near the road's right edge and signal about one hundred feet beforehand. Stop before the limit line, otherwise before the crosswalk, or otherwise before the intersection. A right turn after stopping at red is allowed unless a sign forbids it; a red arrow requires waiting for green. Cross a bus lane only to make the right turn, and do not drive, stop, park or leave a vehicle there [A06].
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R05; confusables sec06-F12, sec06-F13, sec06-F14 [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A07
Dedicated right-turn lanes skip the stop and beat through-traffic reds yet still obey their own curb signal and yield crosswalks, and left turns mirror the right-turn choreography from the divider with straight wheels until committed [A07].
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R06; confusables sec06-F15, sec06-F16 [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A08
Left on red is legal only from a one-way street onto a one-way street with no ban sign, and U-turns are allowed across double yellows, in residential gaps of two hundred feet, at green lights without posted bans, or through divided-highway openings, while everywhere else on the never list they stay banned [A08].
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R07; confusables sec06-F17, sec06-F18, sec06-F19 [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A09
Diagrammed two-way lefts hug the middle lane both entering and exiting, single-lane rights hug the right edge throughout, and a two-way-to-one-way left starting far left may finish in any open lane once three or more lanes run that way [A09].
Why it matters: group turn-diagrams; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-R07; confusables sec06-F20 [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A10
One-way-to-one-way lefts start far left with cyclists sharing the turn lane and finish anywhere past three lanes, matching rights start far right, T-intersection turns yield to through traffic from the center lane, and braking means coasting off the gas, pressing lightly, and stopping behind limit lines with rear-wheel sight gaps [A10].
Why it matters: group turn-diagrams; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-R09; confusables sec06-F21, sec06-F22 [A10].
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A11
Merging drivers yield to highway traffic by matching speed on the ramp, signaling, checking mirrors and shoulders, and holding three seconds of space without stopping or crossing solids, while exiting drivers signal five seconds ahead in the proper lane at a safe speed [A11].
Why it matters: group merge-exit; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R03; confusables sec06-F23, sec06-F24 [A11].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A12
Entering traffic needs half a block near one hundred fifty feet in town and a full block near three hundred feet on highways, never into a blocked intersection, and passing needs a third of a mile of clear hill or curve while bans cover blind hills, junctions within one hundred feet, crossings, driveways, and missing reentry room [A12].
Why it matters: group gaps-passing; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R11; confusables sec06-F25, sec06-F26 [A12].
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A13
Passing runs signal, shoulder, lane, speed, signal back, right-side passes fit only multi-lane highways, left-turning leaders, and one-way streets, and a driver being passed must hold lane and speed [A13].
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-R12; confusables sec06-F27 [A13].
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A14
Parallel parking wants a space three feet longer than the car, a roughly two-foot offset pull-up with the signal on, a roughly forty-five-degree back-in, and a finish parallel within eighteen inches of the curb with brake set and a careful exit [A14].
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec06-F28 [A14].
Source: [A14 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A15
Straight-line backing signals to the curb, rolls three vehicle lengths within three feet of the curb, then cancels and repeats the checks to leave, while hill parking always sets the brake and gear with wheels biting the curb downhill, facing center uphill, and pointing right where no curb exists [A15].
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R14; confusables sec06-F29, sec06-F30 [A15].
Source: [A15 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A16
At a white curb, stop briefly for passengers; at green, observe the signed or painted time limit. Yellow permits loading passengers or freight only for the posted time, usually with the noncommercial driver remaining present. Red excludes stops, standing and parking except buses in a designated bus zone; blue is reserved for authorized disability placards or plates [A16].
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R15; confusables sec06-F31, sec06-F32 [A16].
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A17
Wrong-side and freeway parking survive only for emergencies, officer orders, or posted permission with freeway stops fully off the pavement and removable after more than four hours, and enforcement stops open with a right signal, a full move to the shoulder, radio off, seated waiting, window down, and hands visible [A17].
Why it matters: group stops; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec06-F33, sec06-F34 [A17].
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A18
Drivers may verbally decline searches but must never resist lawful ones, must produce license, insurance, and registration, treat passenger ID as declinable yet sometimes required, obey seat and exit orders, and save immigration answers for federal officers only [A18].
Why it matters: group rights; difficulty high; prereq sec06-R17; confusables sec06-F35 [A18].
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A19
Recording officers in public is protected when announced and non-interfering with devices untouched and phones locked outside parole, objections stay verbal without physical resistance, and complaints go to the employing agency, which must investigate free of retaliation and bias [A19].
Why it matters: group rights; difficulty medium; prereq sec06-R18; confusables sec06-F36, sec06-F37 [A19].
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ca-c:california-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
